correctness.rationale: The exact domain is all 15-edge subsets of the uniquely specified Petersen graph, checked at each size 0 through 5 (4944 candidates). Two separately constructed graph models (Kneser KG(5,2) and generalized Petersen GP(5,2)) with separately coded locating-dominating tests agree on the unique optimum size 5, 246 states, 1470 exchanges, all-source distance profiles and 90 exception pairs. The first exhausts all 120 S5 permutations. Every vertex/edge/pair and BFS source is checked, not sampled. K_{3,3} follows from ten verified six-state cubic triangle-free defect components. No infinite extrapolation, independent audit, or unproved claim of external certification is used.

value.rationale: Optimal sensor or edge detector placements are naturally reconfigured by replacing one chosen edge while keeping all external edges distinguished. The full optimum solution graph is a natural invariant rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. Its 246-state four-orbit classification, sharp worst-case one-extra-exchange bound, and ten canonical K_{3,3} geodesic obstructions explain exactly where direct Johnson-geodesic transformation fails. Known single optimum identifying codes and generic domination bounds do not determine this operational geometry; it is useful as an exact benchmark and a structural finite boundary for location-domination reconfiguration.
